data.why: The app's 'Try the example' button (js/wbdemo.js) generates a synthetic cut-membrane, multi-exposure western blot dataset entirely in the browser; no files need to be uploaded or written.

goals: Assemble a publication-ready western blot figure from raw exposure and marker photos of one experiment
Group exposures and marker pictures by membrane, confirm detected strips and their tilt, and adjust protein boxes
Pick the best (unsaturated, high-signal) exposure for each protein row and verify no saturation
Calibrate molecular weight by clicking ladder bands on the marker picture
Label lanes and proteins, add condition rows, and arrange an optional multi-column layout
Run the pre-flight check and export a publication figure (PNG/TIFF/SVG) plus densitometry CSV and processing log

review.summary: The tree follows BlotFigure's five-step path from raw exposures to an exported figure faithfully, and every screen I sampled supports its node. It leaves out the core box-and-lane adjustment work of step 3, saving the project, and the supplementary/integrity exports, so it needs those added and a few nodes regrouped before filing.
